html:
The Sultanate of Utetera was the trading state the Zanzibari merchant Tippu Tip built in the eastern Congo basin in the second half of the 1800s, with its capital at Kasongo on the Lualaba River. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900; Utetera was the land of the Tetela people.

Tippu Tip and his armed caravans took ivory and slaves by raiding and by trade, and sent them east to Zanzibar. His rule reached from the Lualaba toward the Kasai and the Aruwimi. He helped Henry Morton Stanley on his crossing of Africa in 1876 and 1877.

In 1887 Leopold II made him governor of the Stanley Falls district for the Congo Free State. Tippu Tip left for Zanzibar in 1890. Two years later his son Sefu and the other Arab Swahili leaders went to war with the Free State, and by 1894 they were defeated in the Congo Arab war.
